nodes.label: Binding hot spot
nodes.summary: Small sub-region of a pocket contributing disproportionately to binding free energy; found via fragment screening or computational fragment mapping.

nodes.label: Pharmacophore
nodes.summary: 3D arrangement of features (H-bond donor/acceptor, hydrophobe, aromatic, charge) required for a ligand to bind; often built by anchoring to hot spots.

nodes.label: Water displacement
nodes.summary: Displacing an ordered, enthalpically unhappy water from the pocket can yield a large affinity gain independent of the ligand's own direct interactions.
nodes.source_note: General medicinal-chemistry knowledge - not tied to a single paper turned up in search; standard SBDD textbook concept.

nodes.label: Shape complementarity
nodes.summary: Geometric fit between ligand and pocket; necessary but not sufficient for affinity - overweighted by naive scoring functions.
nodes.source_note: General medicinal-chemistry knowledge - not tied to a single paper turned up in search.

nodes.label: Electrostatic complementarity
nodes.summary: Alignment of ligand/pocket charge and H-bond donor-acceptor patterns; usually the dominant term once shape is roughly satisfied.
nodes.source_note: General medicinal-chemistry knowledge - not tied to a single paper turned up in search.

nodes.label: Induced fit
nodes.summary: Pocket/loop conformational change upon ligand binding; apo structures can misrepresent the true holo pocket.
nodes.source_note: General structural-biology knowledge - not tied to a single paper turned up in search.

nodes.label: Cryptic pocket
nodes.summary: Binding site not visible/open in the unliganded (apo) structure, only forms upon ligand engagement.
nodes.source_note: General structural-biology knowledge - not tied to a single paper turned up in search.

nodes.label: Pocket flexibility / plasticity
nodes.summary: How much a pocket's volume/shape varies across structures or an MD trajectory, not just atomic wobble within one static structure (e.g. PXR's unusually plastic pocket). Quantified as a plasticity score (normalized pocket-volume range across superposed structures or MD frames); drives whether rigid or ensemble docking is valid, and should discount per-fragment confidence when only one rigid structure was used.
nodes.source_note: General structural-biology knowledge, grounded in the PXR case discussed in this session - not tied to a single paper.

nodes.label: Rigid-receptor docking (limitation)
nodes.summary: Standard docking approximation holding the protein fixed while sampling only ligand pose/conformation; breaks down under induced fit or cryptic pockets.
nodes.source_note: Review discusses docking limitations generally; not specific to this failure mode by name.

nodes.label: Scoring function limitations
nodes.summary: Docking scoring functions are fast empirical/knowledge-based approximations to binding free energy; often poor at ranking hits by affinity even when pose prediction is good.

nodes.label: Binding free energy (dG)
nodes.summary: The thermodynamic quantity determining affinity; decomposes into enthalpic (H-bonds, vdW, electrostatics) and entropic (conformational, solvent release) terms.
nodes.source_note: Standard thermodynamics/textbook concept - not tied to a single paper turned up in search.

nodes.label: Free energy perturbation (FEP)
nodes.summary: Rigorous but expensive alchemical method to compute relative binding free energy differences between ligands.
nodes.source_note: General computational-chemistry knowledge - not tied to a single paper turned up in search.

nodes.label: Druggability
nodes.summary: Assessment of whether a pocket is likely to bind a small molecule with high affinity - based on volume, hydrophobicity, enclosure, and hot-spot hit-rate in fragment screens.

nodes.label: Ensemble docking
nodes.summary: Docking against multiple receptor conformations (from MD, NMR, or multiple crystal structures) to partly account for flexibility rigid docking misses.
nodes.source_note: General computational-chemistry knowledge - not tied to a single paper turned up in search.

nodes.label: Molecular docking
nodes.summary: Computational sampling of ligand poses in a binding site with a scoring-function estimate of affinity; fast first-pass triage.

nodes.label: Fragment-based screening
nodes.summary: Screening small (~150-250 Da) fragment libraries by NMR/X-ray/SPR to directly identify hot spots and build up ligands atom-by-atom.

nodes.label: MD refinement
nodes.summary: Post-docking molecular dynamics used to relax a docked pose, check pose stability, and estimate free energy more rigorously (e.g. MM-GBSA).

nodes.label: MDpocket
nodes.summary: fpocket-based tool that tracks cavity volume, shape, and opening/closing across an MD trajectory or other conformational ensemble, instead of a single static structure.

nodes.label: Exploring protein hotspots by optimized fragment pharmacophores
nodes.summary: Nature Communications 2021. Fragment-pharmacophore method for locating and characterizing protein binding hot spots.

nodes.label: Fragment-based identification of druggable 'hot spots' of proteins
nodes.summary: Bioinformatics 2009. Computational fragment-mapping approach to hot spot / druggability prediction.

nodes.label: Challenges, Applications, and Recent Advances of Protein-Ligand Docking in Structure-Based Drug Design
nodes.summary: Review covering docking scoring-function and sampling limitations.

nodes.label: Protein structure-based drug design: from docking to molecular dynamics
nodes.summary: Current Opinion in Structural Biology review on moving from a naive dock to MD-based refinement and free-energy estimation.

nodes.label: A Practical Guide to Molecular Docking and Homology Modelling for Medicinal Chemists
nodes.summary: Introductory, chemist-facing guide to running and sanity-checking docking/homology modelling.

plasticity score above threshold makes ensemble docking mandatory
